paragraphs.title: Tola and Jair: Leaders of Israel

easy.explanation: Tola the son of Puah arose after Abimelech to defend Israel.
easy.q: Who arose after Abimelech to defend Israel?

easy.explanation: Tola judged Israel twenty and three years.
easy.q: How many years did Tola judge Israel?
How many sons did Jair have?

answers: They were associated with Jair and the land of Gilead
They were where Tola was buried
medium.explanation: The towns were called Havoth-jair and were in the land of Gilead.
medium.q: What does the name Havoth-jair show about the towns?

medium.explanation: Here, judging Israel means leading and governing the people.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “judged Israel” mean?

answers: Tola after Abimelech, and Jair after Tola
Tola and Jair led at the same time
medium.explanation: Tola arose after Abimelech, and Jair arose after Tola.
medium.q: Which sequence correctly describes the leaders?

answers: His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys
The thirty towns were called Havoth-jair
Jair was buried in each town
challenge.explanation: The thirty towns were called Havoth-jair unto that day.
challenge.q: What detail connects Jair with the towns in Gilead?

answers: Jair was closely connected with the region of Gilead
challenge.explanation: These details emphasize Jair’s connection with Gilead.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jair’s thirty sons, thirty ass colts, and thirty cities?

challenge.explanation: The passage says that Jair was buried in Camon.

paragraphs.title: Sin and Oppression by Neighboring Peoples

answers: Baalim, Ashtaroth, and the gods of many surrounding peoples
easy.explanation: Israel served many foreign gods and forsook the LORD.
easy.q: Whom did the children of Israel serve instead of the LORD?

answers: The Philistines and the children of Ammon
easy.explanation: The LORD sold Israel into the hands of the Philistines and the children of Ammon.
easy.q: Into whose hands did the LORD sell Israel?

easy.explanation: They were vexed and oppressed for eighteen years.
easy.q: How long were the Israelites oppressed in the passage?

answers: They forsook the LORD and served other gods
They failed to build cities in Gilead
medium.explanation: The passage connects Israel’s oppression with forsaking the LORD and serving idols.
medium.q: What was the stated reason for Israel’s oppression?

answers: They abandoned the LORD and stopped serving Him
medium.explanation: To forsake the LORD means to abandon Him and no longer serve Him.
medium.q: What does “forsook the LORD” mean in this passage?

answers: The Ammonites remained only east of Jordan
The Ammonites crossed Jordan and fought Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim
The Philistines crossed Jordan and attacked only Gilead
medium.explanation: The Ammonites crossed Jordan to fight Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim.
medium.q: How did the danger spread to additional Israelites?

answers: The extent of Israel’s abandonment and idolatry
The number of judges in Israel
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes that Israel served many foreign gods instead of the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the long list of foreign gods emphasize?

answers: On the other side of Jordan in the land of the Amorites, in Gilead
challenge.explanation: The oppression affected Israel on the other side of Jordan in Gilead.
challenge.q: Where were the Israelites oppressed for eighteen years?

answers: The threat spread to more regions and tribes
challenge.explanation: Their attacks on Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim show that the threat had expanded.
challenge.q: What does the Ammonites’ crossing Jordan show about Israel’s situation?

paragraphs.title: Israel’s Cry and the LORD’s Response

answers: They had sinned and served Baalim
They had chosen a new leader
easy.explanation: They confessed, “We have sinned against thee,” and admitted serving Baalim.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel confess when they cried unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD told them to cry unto the gods they had chosen.
easy.q: To whom did the LORD first direct Israel in its trouble?

answers: They put away the strange gods and served the LORD
easy.explanation: They removed the strange gods from among them and served the LORD.
easy.q: What did the children of Israel do after the LORD’s words?

answers: Deliverances from Egypt and several surrounding peoples
The burial of Jair in Camon
medium.explanation: The LORD recalled delivering Israel from Egypt, the Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines, and others.
medium.q: What past deliverances did the LORD remind Israel of?

answers: I rescued you from their power
I sent you to fight them
medium.explanation: The LORD was reminding Israel that He had rescued them from their enemies.
medium.q: What does “I delivered you out of their hand” mean?

answers: Israel removed the strange gods and served the LORD
Israel asked the princes of Gilead for a leader
medium.explanation: Israel put away the strange gods and returned to serving the LORD.
medium.q: What change occurred before the LORD’s soul was grieved for Israel’s misery?

answers: He recalls His past deliverances while rebuking Israel for forsaking Him
He praises Israel’s worship of idols
He commands Israel to leave Gilead
challenge.explanation: The LORD remembers rescuing Israel but also rebukes them for abandoning Him.
challenge.q: What tension appears in the LORD’s response to Israel?

answers: They continue to defend their idolatry
They accept the LORD’s correction and ask for deliverance
They declare that they need no help
challenge.explanation: Israel acknowledges its sin and asks the LORD to deliver them.
challenge.q: What does Israel’s request, “Do thou unto us whatsoever seemeth good unto thee,” suggest?

answers: It showed a practical change and a return to serving the LORD
It caused Israel to serve the Ammonites
It was done only by the princes of Gilead
challenge.explanation: Removing the idols demonstrated repentance and renewed service to the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the significance of Israel putting away the strange gods?

paragraphs.title: Preparing for War and Seeking a Leader

easy.explanation: The children of Ammon gathered and encamped in Gilead.
easy.q: Where did the children of Ammon encamp?

easy.explanation: The children of Israel assembled and encamped in Mizpeh.
easy.q: Where did the children of Israel encamp?

answers: A leader who would begin fighting the Ammonites
easy.explanation: They sought a man who would begin the fight and become head over Gilead.
easy.q: What were the princes of Gilead seeking?

answers: Both sides were preparing for conflict
Both sides were leaving the land
medium.explanation: The Ammonites and Israelites had gathered in separate camps before the battle.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the two camps mentioned in these verses?

medium.explanation: The phrase means to start fighting against the Ammonites.
medium.q: What does “begin to fight” mean in this context?

answers: To lead the fight against the children of Ammon
medium.explanation: They wanted a leader who would direct the people in battle.
medium.q: Why did the princes of Gilead seek a man to be head?

answers: The gathered forces needed someone to organize and lead them
challenge.explanation: After assembling, the people recognized the need for a commander.
challenge.q: What does the movement from gathering the armies to seeking a leader show?

answers: He would lead all the inhabitants of Gilead
He would be only a messenger to Ammon
He would judge only in Shamir
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes leadership over all the people of Gilead.
challenge.q: What does “he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead” mean?

answers: Ammon was encamped in Gilead and Israel was encamped in Mizpeh
challenge.explanation: The presence of both camps shows that a confrontation was near.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the danger was immediate?
